description.narrative: The Road Maintenance Project for Paraguay will establish a sustainable road management strategy that ensures the upgrading and maintenance of the road network through a rational and balanced use of scarce resources. The project consists of the following components: Component 1: will finance the strengthening of strategic planning, road conservation, and budget management within a framework of fiscal constraints; in particular, it will support a series of consulting services, training and goods. Component 2: this component has two subcomponents which complement each other (i) performance based contracts; (ii) toll system optimization. Component 3: will finance the rehabilitation and conservation of unpaved national roads that connect to the national paved network, and secondary roads connecting rural communities to these; and propose a comprehensive solution for improved access to isolated rural communities.

The project's development objective is to establish a sustainable road management strategy that ensures the upgrading and maintenance of the road network through a rational and balanced use of scarce resources.

comment.narrative: Partially achieved with delay. System was established under the Project, being effectively utilized to measure compliance with the Road Strategy.  A system of regular and permanent traffic counting is now in place, starting from 2014. . All paved network is part of the inventory and 50% of the unpaved network.

title.narrative: Road strategy and five year plan implemented

Road strategy as approved in December 2006 and the five year plan was prepared and is now under implementation.  The strategy has helped increase the percentage of paved roads and improve the overall condition of the road network.  MOPC is in a position to provide a new and updated five year plan based on inputs provided through the Project.

title.narrative: Component 3- Vehicle operating cost-truck: San Pedro, Caazapa, Caaguazu (Guarani per veh-km)

comment.narrative: Expected to be Achieved. Target VOC were significantly reduced as part of the January 2014 restructuring based on revised, actual data for 2013 as follows:. 11483 (San Pedro), 11283 (Caazapa) and 11360 (Caaguazu).  Final actual for Vehicle Operating Cost will be confirmed by the MOPC by project closing.  The average vehicle operating cost for a large truck is reported as 10, 367.74 country wide. The actual breakdown by department is pending but based on the estimates for the country the target has been met.

title.narrative: Percentage of users reporting satisfaction with the quality of the roads (San Pedro, Caazapa and Caaguazu road segments)

comment.narrative: The user satisfaction surveys have been carried out and results will be presented to the Government by June 30, 2016. After January 22, 2014 restructuring, this indicator only applies to beneficiaries in the three departments where non-paved roads are toe improved.  The following were the reported levels of satisfaction:  7% good, 28% fair and 65% bad as a baseline.

comment.narrative: Partly achieved. 6 micro-enterprises had been created at the time of the January 2014 restructuring when this indicator was added. No further micro-enterprises were created before the end of the Project because of budget limitations.
